findings.where: The 'coming soon' notice near the foot of the page (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The notice sits on a saturated red ground that is not in the palette. On a page with no other alarm colour, it looks like an error banner or a warning that something has failed. All it actually says is that listings are on their way. The rules file names this block as the interior announcement, which takes the ink night ground.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker scrolling to the end would read it as something going wrong with the site or the destination, not as calm launch news. The founder would object because red here contradicts the semantic palette. It also undercuts 'effortless' and 'calm machine'.

findings.fault: The twelve static tags are filled with a rainbow of off-palette colours: yellow, green, pink, purple, blue and a coral-like red. Each also has a border in a different, clashing colour, such as a pink fill with a blue edge or a yellow fill with a coral edge. The colours encode nothing, yet varied colour suggests a category key. The coral-red fills also borrow the colour the brand reserves for its one action per view.
findings.who_objects: A visitor would look for what the colours mean and find nothing. The founder would object because the brand gives each colour one job and keeps purple and pink out of the palette, and coral is for CTAs only. The cluster is the loudest thing on the page, but the loudness is noise rather than a claim.

findings.fault: This one heading is set in turquoise, italic and underlined. Every other heading is ink. Turquoise is a fill colour with no text-safe role, and here it takes on a link's colour treatment on a static heading.
findings.who_objects: A reader would take it for a link or a special state when it is just one of four equal sections. The founder would object because the rules bar raw fill colours as type, and like headings should be treated alike.

findings.where: Top of the page, from the title block through the intro
findings.fault: The destination page opens straight on flat sand with no turquoise day-hero ground. The rules file names the destination-page top banner as the loud marketing zone. As built, the whole page reads at working-area volume.
findings.who_objects: The founder would object because 'sterile' is the brand's named enemy and destination banners are meant to carry its energy. A visitor gets a plain document rather than a beachy guide.
